predecessors.name: Federal Republic of Central America
predecessors.text: eight departments in western present-day Guatemala (Totonicapán, Huehuetenango, Quetzaltenango, San Marcos, Retalhuleu, Suchitepéquez, Sololá, Quiché) plus the Soconusco region of Chiapas

successors.name: Guatemala
successors.text: the eight departments of western Guatemala (Totonicapán, Huehuetenango, Quetzaltenango, San Marcos, Retalhuleu, Suchitepéquez, Sololá, Quiché)

successors.name: Centralist Republic of Mexico
successors.text: the Soconusco region of Chiapas (about 4,700-5,800 km2 on the Soconusco page), drawn as a radius around Tapachula

ledger.x: 1838: Los Altos proclaims independence from Guatemala at Quetzaltenango.
1840: Carrera retakes Quetzaltenango and ends the first Los Altos.
1849: Carrera ends Los Altos for good.
1849: Los Altos is reincorporated into Guatemala; its land goes to the Guatemalan state.

wars.name: Guatemalan reconquest of Los Altos
wars.outcome: Guatemala 'resorted to force'; Carrera entered Quetzaltenango on 2 April 1840 and annexed Los Altos back into Guatemala.

wars.name: Carrera's second reconquest of Los Altos
wars.outcome: Los Altos declared independence again on 26 August 1848 and was reincorporated on 8 May 1849 when Carrera 'took Quetzaltenango and remained in the plaza'.

certainty.note: The Los Altos page defines the state by departments, not by a surveyed frontier; the Soconusco boundary with Guatemala was only fixed by the 1882 treaty (Soconusco page).
